note: Views Arg Order Sort adds a Views sort handler (UI label 'Multi-item Argument Order', plugin id views_arg_order_sort_default, declared via hook_views_data as a #global sort on table views_arg_order_sort field weight) that orders rows to match the order of values in a chosen multi-item contextual filter by building a CASE ... WHEN ... THEN <pos> expression. Options: argument_number (0-indexed contextual filter), inherit_type (derive column from that argument), field_type (table::field like node::nid when not inheriting), null_below, and standard order (DESC reverses). No configure route, permission, Drush; all state lives in a view config entity's display sorts. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real view config: introspection reads the sort's plugin id / field_type; execution adds the sort to a view's display with a given argument_number or explicit field_type, verified against the live views.view config.

evals.prompt: In Views, I pass a list of node IDs like 5,3,9 into a contextual filter and want the results returned in that exact order using the views_arg_order_sort module. Which Views sort do I add (its UI label or plugin id)?
evals.expected_output: Add the 'Multi-item Argument Order' sort criterion (plugin id views_arg_order_sort_default). It builds a CASE expression so rows sort by their position in the argument values.

evals.prompt: For the views_arg_order_sort 'Multi-item Argument Order' sort, how do I tell it which contextual filter to read, and how does it know which database column to sort on?
evals.expected_output: argument_number (0-indexed) selects which contextual filter's values to use. With inherit_type on (default) it derives the sort column from that argument's own handler; turn inherit_type off to set an explicit field_type like node::nid. null_below places non-matching rows at the end, and a DESC order reverses the argument sequence.

evals.prompt: How does views_arg_order_sort actually make the query return rows in the order of the passed argument values?
evals.expected_output: Its query() splits the chosen argument's values (on + or ,) and emits an ORDER BY CASE <col> WHEN <val0> THEN 0 WHEN <val1> THEN 1 ... ELSE <null_o> END, so each row sorts by its position in the argument list; non-matching rows go first or last depending on null_below and direction.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the view with machine id 'vaos_intro_view' has a sort added by the views_arg_order_sort module. Inspect the live view configuration and give the sort plugin id it uses.
evals.expected_output: views_arg_order_sort_default (the 'Multi-item Argument Order' sort), in vaos_intro_view's display sorts.

evals.prompt: The view 'vaos_intro_view' on this site has a Multi-item Argument Order sort configured with 'inherit type' turned off and an explicit argument field type. Inspect the live view configuration and give that field_type value.
evals.expected_output: field_type is 'node::nid' (inherit_type: false) on the views_arg_order_sort_default sort in vaos_intro_view.

evals.prompt: The view with machine id 'vaos_task_view' on this site has a Content: ID contextual filter (the first argument). Using the views_arg_order_sort module, add a 'Multi-item Argument Order' sort to its default display that orders results by the values of that first contextual filter (argument_number 1), inheriting the field type from the argument. Apply the change to the live view.
evals.expected_output: views.view.vaos_task_view default display sorts contains a handler with plugin_id: views_arg_order_sort_default (table views_arg_order_sort, field weight) and argument_number: 1 (inherit_type on).

evals.prompt: On the view with machine id 'vaos_task_view', add a views_arg_order_sort 'Multi-item Argument Order' sort to the default display, but with 'inherit type of field from argument' turned OFF and the explicit argument field type set to node::nid. Apply the change to the live view.
evals.expected_output: views.view.vaos_task_view default display sorts contains a handler with plugin_id: views_arg_order_sort_default, inherit_type: false, field_type: 'node::nid'.
